Hero.comment: The loading screen only plays in the first seconds after a full page load.

Intro.comment: The home page: who I am in one screen, a short introduction, three featured projects, a band of screens from every project, what I build, and the tools I use.

ProjectCard.comment: Glass project card with a soft gold spotlight that follows the cursor. The whole card opens the project page.

ParallaxGallery.comment: A full-width band of tall photo tiles in four columns (two on phones). As it scrolls past, each column slides at its own speed. With reduced motion it is a plain, still grid. The photos are whatever is in public/images/gallery (see galleryImages in src/lib/gallery.ts); they're decoration, so no links.

ExpertiseList.comment: The list of services, drawn for a light (matte) panel. Hovering a row turns it dark and floats a matching project screenshot beside the cursor.

Marquee.comment: An endless ticker on a glossy amethyst band, set at a slight angle. The second copy makes the loop seamless; hovering pauses it.

ProjectStack.comment: Projects stacked like cards: each one slides up over the last as you scroll.

ProjectIntro.comment: Top of a project page: the project's reel fills the whole first screen behind it, and the title, what it is and what it's built with sit in the middle in large, heavy type.

ShotRail.comment:
A project's screens as a strip that drifts sideways on its own.
- Pointing at a screen (or tapping it) slows the strip to a stop, brings that screen forward and lets the others dim and blur; moving away sets it drifting again.
- Tapping or clicking the focused screen opens it full size (ShotViewer).
- To look through faster, drag or swipe the strip, scroll sideways on a trackpad, or use the arrow buttons. It glides on from a flick, then settles back into its own drift. With reduced motion it is a plain row you can scroll.

Footer.comment: Closing section on every page: a glass card with a call to action, a one-click way to copy the email address, and the site's links.

Assistant.comment:
Mira: a friendly assistant who collects a short project brief, one question at a time. She says each line aloud while it types out, and the orb moves with her voice and shows her mood.
 Two brains can write her lines. The scripted one (src/lib/miraBrain.ts) uses her written, recorded lines and always works. When a Gemini key is set up, the live one (/api/mira) words her replies and understands typed messages; if it is slow or fails, the scripted one answers that turn instead.
 Where the conversation is (welcome, asking, thinking, sending…) is one state machine: src/lib/miraMachine.ts. This component reads its phase and sends it events; it never sets the phase directly. The phase and step are also on the section as data-phase / data-step / data-ready, for tests and debugging.
